text:
Nora (support): FYI — multiple customers hitting 5xx on hosted inference /v1/generate since ~09:40 PST. Errors look like 502/504 from the control plane gateway. One customer posted trace id `trace-20260315-09:42-az1` and a few more in the ticket. No billing breaks reported yet but API is failing for live traffic. :rotating_light:

Maya (support): Observed ~25% error rate increase across regions us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate, sometimes gets `502 Bad Gateway` with body: `{
  "error": "upstream_error",
  "message": "control-plane dependency failed: routing-policy"
}`. Customers complaining about timeouts too.

Liam (sre-oncall): digging in. Early signs point to control-plane dependencies timing out. I can see a spike in requests to routing-policy and session-store failing (timeouts/500s). Paging eng-runtime.

Liam (sre-oncall): logs snippet from gateway at 09:41:
```
[2026-03-15T09:41:12Z] gateway: upstream request to controlplane/routing-policy timed out after 5s, trace=trace-20260315-09:41-xy2
[2026-03-15T09:41:12Z] gateway: returning 502 to client, reason=upstream_timeout
```

Arjun (eng-runtime): we had a routing-policy deploy at 09:30 (rolled to canary then prod). DeployBot shows rollout completed at 09:33. I'm seeing routing-policy instances logging SQL timeouts to config-db and session-store (redis) connection errors.

DeployBot: rollout routing-policy v2.14.0 -> promoted to prod at 2026-03-15T09:33:21Z (ci-build 8192).

Maya (support): customers include tenant ids: t-451, t-892, t-301. All reported same 502 body with differing trace ids. Tickets linked: #CUST-2034, #CUST-2036, #CUST-2037.

Liam (sre-oncall): checking metrics: config-db p95 query latency jumped from 35ms -> 1.2s at 09:30. Routing-policy 5xx rate spiked to 40% for 3 minutes. Session-store (redis) connection errors increased concurrently.

Arjun (eng-runtime): log from routing-policy:
```
2026-03-15T09:31:02.123Z ERROR routing_policy.handler - failed to fetch policy for tenant t-451: psycopg2.errors.QueryCanceled: canceling statement due to statement timeout
2026-03-15T09:31:02.124Z ERROR routing_policy.cache - redis error: ConnectionResetError: socket connection broken
```

Liam (sre-oncall): hypothesis: the new routing-policy change introduced a heavier query pattern that hit config-db and surfaced long-running queries + exhausted redis pool leading to cascading 5xx at the gateway.

Nora (support): immediate customer communication: posted interim update to tickets, asked customers to retry after 10-15m and offered dedicated routing if needed. Also asked for logs and sample curl reproducer.

Maya (support): repro curl we asked customers to run:
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Trace-Id: trace-20260315-09:42-test' -d '{"input":"hello"}' --max-time 10
```
They get `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` with gateway body above.

Liam (sre-oncall): temporary mitigation suggestions: revert routing-policy to previous version (v2.13.7), or increase DB statement_timeout and enlarge redis connection pool as stopgap. Also suggest gateway circuit-breaker to fallback to default policy rather than blocking.

Arjun (eng-runtime): I recommend rollback — new policy adds a join that ends up doing a seq scan in worst-case for some tenants. I'll prepare rollback. Also will add a quick cache bypass so heavy queries hit a read-replica with longer timeout rather than primary.

DevOpsBot: rollback request queued: routing-policy -> v2.13.7, initiated by @arjun at 2026-03-15T09:55:04Z.

Liam (sre-oncall): applying temporary rate-limiting on control-plane calls from gateway to routing-policy to reduce storming. Command we ran: `kubectl scale deployment/gateway --replicas=4 -n controlplane` and `kubectl patch configmap/gateway-cb --patch '{"data":{"routing_policy_threshold":"0.7"}}'` (ops only).

Arjun (eng-runtime): rollback completed at 10:15. DeployBot confirms.

DeployBot: routing-policy v2.13.7 promoted to prod at 2026-03-15T10:15:12Z (rollback by arjun).

Liam (sre-oncall): post-rollback metrics: config-db p95 back to ~40ms, routing-policy 5xx rate down to <1%, session-store errors dropped. Gateway 502s returned to baseline.

Nora (support): updated customers at 10:22 — they confirmed recovery in most cases, one tenant still reporting a couple of spikes; asked to collect traces if it persists.

Maya (support): action items for follow-up:
- eng-runtime to root cause the query pattern and add better fallbacks/circuit-breaker behavior (assigned Arjun)
- infra to review redis pool sizing and DB read-replica routing under heavy joins (assigned SRE)
- support to add automated status page note and follow up customers whose SLA impacted (assigned Nora/Maya)

Arjun (eng-runtime): next steps from our side: add query plan monitoring for routing-policy, add tenant-level query timeouts, add graceful fallback to default routing policy when dependent services slow. We'll post a PR with fixes and a canary plan.

Liam (sre-oncall): I'll keep watch for 2h and alert if residual errors >1% of baseline. Created incident INC-20260315-02.

Nora (support): thanks team. Closing the live escalation thread; will reopen if any customer reports persistent 5xx. :thumbsup:
